Thanks again for taking time this morning - great discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Goal: validate p50/p95/p99 latency across US/EU/APAC for your interactive use cases and confirm data residency options for EU workloads.
- Current ask: run controlled latency tests from your locations + enable a short PoC that mirrors production request patterns.

What we shared on the call:
- Initial synthetic results (attached) showing p99 under 220ms in US, ~240ms in EU, ~290ms APAC for a 1k token end-to-end request on our hosted endpoints.
- Differentiators vs hyperscalers we discussed: dedicated capacity option, smart routing with regional fallbacks, KV prefix caching, and transparent per-token cost breakdowns.

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll provide a test plan + short script you can run from your EU and APAC offices (attachment: test-plan-poc.csv).
2) Camila will run parallel synthetic tests from our EU and APAC infra and share dashboards by EOD.
3) If numbers look good, Marissa will scope a 30-90 day dedicated trial for predictable throughput and data residency controls.
4) Please confirm preferred test windows and any IPs to whitelist.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-eu-us-apac-20260829.pdf, test-plan-poc.csv, redwood-vs-hyperscalers-one-pager.pdf

Proposed meeting: 45m sync Wed 8/31 10am PT to review results - does that work for you?

Thanks - Jordan

Alex - adding a couple of procurement / competitive notes so you have context before we run tests: 

Competitive TL;DR vs hyperscalers:
- Dedicated capacity vs Bedrock/Vertex endpoints: gives predictable p99 under commit; hyperscalers often route to multi-tenant endpoints with less predictable tail latency.
- Data residency: our Private deployment supports full EU-only control plane with customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we can include DPA language for your legal team.
- Cost: we provide detailed per-token and per-route cost breakdowns; for your transactional workloads this can materially reduce unit cost vs always-hosted hyperscaler endpoints.

Procurement & next steps:
- If tests validate performance, we can provision a 90-day dedicated trial (discounted) to validate production load and residency.
- For SOC2 and the security pack: Jordan / I will send over the certs and pentest summary via the secure link (I'll share after this thread).

Kicked off the synthetic runs from APAC and EU nodes at 22:05 SGT and 09:00 CEST respectively. Early results pushed to the Datadog dashboard - link above. Preliminary observations: 

- APAC: median ~260ms, p95 ~340ms, p99 ~420ms for the 1k-token shape (streaming off).
- EU: median ~230ms, p95 ~275ms, p99 ~315ms.
- Discrepancy notes: APAC tail is influenced by larger token counts and our current nearest-edge cold starts; warm runs drop p99 ~70-90ms.

I uploaded the full run PDF (redwood-benchmark-eu-us-apac-20260829.pdf) and the raw CSVs to the Drive link. I'll keep this thread updated as we run the real request-shape traces you provide.
